judgments.reasoning_cat1: The wording itself is short and definite: an identified party, a defined trigger ("without cause"), a fixed notice period (90 days) and a required form (prior written notice). The only softness is that it is labelled paragraph "A" of a termination section and says nothing about the effect of termination on accrued pay, benefits or the pension contributions; but no single term in it carries two reasonable meanings. Modest probability only because "without cause" sits implicitly against a for-cause regime elsewhere and the paragraph does not say whether the 90-day notice can be shortened or paid out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This clause is the hinge of the instrument's outward-pointing provisions and is hard to harmonise with several of them. Article I fixes a definite term running from October 5, 2002 "through October 4, 2007," and Article II fixes a five-year maximum payable; a unilateral at-will exit conflicts in operation with that fixed-term structure. Article IV Section 3 supplies a review and appeal process for "corrective action or terminat[ion] for cause," Article V Section 13 permits immediate termination on restriction of medical staff privileges, and Article V Section 15 gives the County a separate 30-day non-appropriation termination right — so termination rights are scattered across Articles IV and V without any priority or "notwithstanding" language reconciling them, and this paragraph (A) plainly presupposes companion paragraphs it does not reproduce. That is a genuine whole-instrument coherence problem about who may end the contract, on what notice, and with what review.
judgments.clause_name: Article IV, Section 1 — Termination of Agreement (para. A)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two textual features raise the risk. First, the cumulation language is entirely one-sided: it preserves only rights "conferred on or reserved to County," saying nothing about the physician's remedies, so a court is invited to read it as excluding (expressio unius) or as merely silent about the physician's remedies. Second, the catch-all string — "any other right or remedy herein or by law or equity provided or permitted ... now or hereafter existing by law or in equity or by statute or otherwise" — ends in an open "or otherwise" whose reach against the enumerated sources is uncertain. Those are namable general-vs-specific and one-sided-drafting tensions, though the sentence's core meaning (remedies are cumulative, not exclusive) is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The clause exposes conflict with the instrument's other remedial machinery. Article IV Section 3 channels "review and appeal of the decision to impose corrective action or terminate for cause" into the Faculty Practice Board policy or the medical staff bylaws — a procedure that reads as the applicable route, while this section preserves every remedy "concurrently" and thus arguably lets the County bypass it. It also overlaps with Article V Section 17 (non-waiver), which separately says the County may "invoke any remedy available ... under this Agreement or by law or in equity," duplicating and potentially varying this section. Its County-only orientation also sits awkwardly with Article V Section 4's instruction that the Agreement be construed as jointly prepared and against neither party.
judgments.clause_name: Article V, Section 11 — Enforcement of Remedies

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short authority recital with a specific statutory citation (Government Code section 31000) and a definite object (contracting with specially trained persons and paying compensation). "Specially trained persons" is a statutory phrase, not an ambiguity the parties created. Nothing in the wording is genuinely susceptible of two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Government Code section 31000 is the authority for contracting for special services, which conventionally connotes an independent contract rather than employment; yet Article V Section 10 states flatly that "Core Physician shall be employed by the County of Kern," and Article III confers County employee-style benefits, leave, pension and health insurance. That is a recital-versus-operative-terms tension over the very nature of the relationship, which is why I put this above the boilerplate baseline, though a court could easily harmonise the two by treating section 31000 as bare authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A purpose recital in plain terms: the County needs professional medical services at KMC unavailable from its own resources. "Unavailable from County resources" is a factual predicate, not an operative standard anyone must apply, so vagueness carries no consequence here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the recital points outward except to the services promised in Article I Section 2 and Exhibit A, with which it is consistent. No cross-reference, proviso or carve-out that could contradict another provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A qualifications recital followed by the "NOW, THEREFORE" transition. Every element (special training, California licensure, qualification to render medical services) is definite and verifiable; no term bears competing meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article V Section 8 (maintaining state and federal licensure) and Article V Section 13 (medical staff membership requirements). Nothing here contradicts an operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Dates and identifiers are wholly specific: the prior agreement is identified by number and date and terminated effective October 5, 2002, and this Agreement runs from October 5, 2002 through October 4, 2007. No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The fixed five-year term is in tension with Article IV Section 1.A's at-will 90-day termination right and with the various other termination triggers (Article V Sections 13 and 15), but a court would ordinarily read a term clause as subject to express termination rights, so the tension lies mainly on the termination clause's side rather than here. Otherwise it dovetails with Article II Section 1's five-year maximum payable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence incorporating Exhibit "A" by express reference and attachment. Definite; the content is delegated to a document expressly made part of the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points outward only to Exhibit A, which is supplied and is consistent in subject matter, and to Article V Section 22's confirmation that attachments are part of the entire agreement. The only latent friction is that Exhibit A's hours (48/week) differ from Article II Section 1's "no less than forty [40] hours," but that mismatch is properly charged to those provisions, not to this incorporation clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The dollar figures, biweekly cadence and caps are precise. The soft spot is the parenthetical definition of full-time: "according to AMA survey data for specialty but no less than forty [40] hours per week" — an external, unidentified data set combined with a floor, so the actual required commitment is not fixed by the text. There is also an internal slip: compensation is set biweekly yet withholding is described as taken "from said daily compensation." Those are namable, though neither is fatal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 40-hour floor here squarely collides with Exhibit A's introductory paragraph ("full-time position requiring 48 hours of service, on average, per week") and Exhibit A Section 6 ("A standard workweek will be 48 hours per week ... 2112 worked hours"). Exhibit A is made part of the Agreement by Article I Section 2, so two operative provisions fix the same variable at different numbers. The clause also cross-refers to "base compensation (as defined in Article II, Section 3)" while Article II Section 2.B builds total compensation from three sources, and paragraph C's no-adjustment-without-written-amendment rule sits against Article II Sections 2.F and 3.B, which let the Faculty Practice Board set assessments and step placement administratively.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mostly definitional and architectural, and the defined labels (total Core Physician compensation, compensation plan, Faculty Practice Board) are expressly created. Softness: "potential other income generated due to the individual's status as a physician" is open-ended; the administrative assessment is capped at one percent only "during the first two years of this Agreement," leaving years three through five without any stated limit; and paragraph G's liability coverage carve-out for conduct that does not "arise directly from the performance of this Agreement" turns on an undefined directness standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to itself ("as defined in Article II, Section 2, paragraph B") and interlocks with Sections 3, 4, 5 and 9, and it delegates rule-making to Faculty Practice Board bylaws and the Administrative Policies and Procedures Manual — documents outside the four corners, which strains Article V Section 22's sole-agreement clause and Article V Section 14's written-modification requirement. Paragraph G's indemnity is also framed "as a matter of law ... to the same extent as ... a regular full-time County employee," which leans on the employment characterisation that Recital A (Gov. Code § 31000 special services) cuts against.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated components of base salary are specific (MIA care with a statutory citation, incarcerated patients, teaching, administration), but the list closes with "other activities approved by the CEO of KMC and the Faculty Practice Board," an unbounded fifth item whose reach against the four specifics is uncertain; "as a safety-net provider, partial compensation for under-compensated and uninsured patients" is also indeterminate as to amount. "Full-effort commitment" is used as a governing measure but its criteria are left to a manual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Step placement, full-effort criteria and research compensation are all sent to the "KMC Faculty Practice Administrative Policies and Procedures Manual," an extrinsic document not attached, which is in tension with Article V Section 22 (entire agreement, including attachments) and Article V Section 14 (modification only in a signed writing). It also interacts with Article II Section 1's fixed biweekly figure and no-adjustment-without-amendment rule, since manual-driven step changes would alter base salary administratively.
judgments.clause_name: Article II, 3. BASE SALARY (ITEMS INCLUDED AND METHOD OF PAYMENT)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed, sequenced flow of funds (gross collections to clearing account, less assessment, less overhead, optional departmental pool, remainder as wages). Terms are defined as used and the deduction order is stated. "Minimum performance standards set by the Faculty Practice Board" and the "overhead distribution formula" are delegated but identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Article II Sections 2, 6, 7, 8 and 9 and with Article III Section 9.D's cross-reference back to it. The only outward strain is the same delegation to Faculty Practice Board determinations that sits against the written-amendment clause; no direct contradiction is visible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The catch-all is genuinely awkward: other income "includes, but is not limited to, royalties, grants, speaker fees, professional witness fees, and other nonprofessional fees." The residual category is labelled "nonprofessional" although several enumerated items are professional in character, so the boundary between this category and the "professional fees" of Section 4 is not cleanly drawn. "Income generated due to the individual's status as a physician" is itself a broad test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Professional witness fees" as compensable other income sits uneasily with Article V Section 2, which requires the physician to testify for the County "at no cost to County," credited only as administrative time. It also must be read against Section 4 (professional fees) since the two categories are mutually defined; paragraph C's CMERF carve-out is expressly reconciled with the assessment rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: practice groups contract with KMC, those contracts define responsibilities and funds flow, groups pay their own overhead and set their own reimbursement policies, and the County disclaims responsibility for the amounts claimed. No ambiguous operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with Article II Sections 4, 7 and 8, which likewise distinguish practice groups from sole practitioners. Nothing points to a contradiction, though it presupposes a separate group contract that is not before me.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines sole practitioners, allocates billing cost and overhead to them, and disclaims County responsibility. Paragraph B leaves the overhead amount for KMC space and personnel "to be negotiated with the CEO of KMC" — an agreement to agree, but expressly framed as future negotiation rather than a present ambiguous obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article II Sections 4, 6 and 8, which use the same categories. No contradiction is exposed by its text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence covering the residual class of Core Physicians and assigning them the cost of billing. The class is defined by exclusion from the two categories already defined, so its boundary is determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Slots cleanly between Sections 6 and 7; nothing outward-pointing beyond the billing service arrangement of Section 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite mechanics: annual opt-in by simple majority of the Department's Core Physicians, criteria approved by the Faculty Practice Board, percentage set yearly, quarterly distribution as taxable wages. The purpose phrase ("activities not recognized by other parts of this compensation plan") is broad but is descriptive, not operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly consistent with Article II Section 4.D, which already contemplates the optional Departmental Pool in the professional-fee waterfall. No conflict apparent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-purpose rule fixing the benefits accrual date as the date first "continuously employed by KMC." "Continuously" could be argued over if service had gaps, but the sentence is otherwise definite and expressly overrides the contract date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deliberately decouples the benefits date from the Article I term dates and dovetails with Article III Section 3's references to prior County service (vacation and sick leave crediting "if Core Physician is presently employed by the County of Kern"). That is harmonisation, not conflict.
judgments.clause_name: Article III, 1. EFFECTIVE DATE OF BENEFITS

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: the benefits provided to other regular County employees of KMC, with a stated 20% employee cost share for those hired after April 15, 1997, and an express statement that changes are not a breach. No ambiguous term of consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unilateral-change permission, expressly deemed not a breach, is in mild tension with Article V Section 14 (modification only by signed writing) and Article V Section 22 (sole agreement), but the clause self-consciously anticipates that point by declaring such changes non-breaching, which is how the parallel Sections 4, 7 and 8 of Article III are drafted too.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Highly quantified: accrual rates per pay period, annual and lifetime caps, payment for unused vacation but not sick leave, and advance approval for education leave. The terms are arithmetically definite and internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Educational leave is credited by reference to "the effective date of the Core Physician's employment contract" and its anniversaries, whereas Article III Section 1 fixes the benefits date as the date of first continuous KMC employment — two different reference dates for accrual within the same Article. The paid-leave hours also interact with the 2112-hour annual objective in Exhibit A Section 6. Both are reconcilable, so I keep this modest.
judgments.clause_name: Article III, 3. PAID LEAVE OF ABSENCE

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grants the same unpaid leave rights County policy gives other regular County employees, with an express non-breach provision for policy changes. Short and determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same structural pattern as Article III Sections 2, 7 and 8; the only outward friction is the standing tension between County-policy incorporation and the written-modification and sole-agreement clauses, which the non-breach sentence expressly addresses.
judgments.clause_name: Article III, 4. UNPAID LEAVE OF ABSENCE

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very long but unusually specific: named plan, precise percentages, a full fixed-dollar contribution table keyed to prior-year Compensation bands, statutory limit references, and a stated correction mechanism for excess contributions. Terms like "Compensation," "Plan year" and "complete Plan year of service" are expressly defined by reference to the Plan Document. Residual softness lies in paragraph C's reservation to "substitute another contribution structure ... designed to maximize benefit to Core Physician on a cost-neutral basis," a standard with no measurable boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Twice the section states "Any changes in the Plan Document will control the terms of this Agreement," and paragraph C lets a substitute structure "control the terms of this Agreement." That is a self-declared priority for an extrinsic, unilaterally amendable document, which sits directly against Article V Section 14 (modification in writing only, signed by the parties) and Article V Section 22 (sole agreement; no modification given force except as recited). It also removes the physician from the County retirement association referenced nowhere else and interlocks with Article III Section 6's Social Security exemption, which depends on the Plan remaining a qualified alternative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two declaratory sentences with a fixed date cut-off (March 31, 1986) for the Medicare exemption. The statement of exemption is a legal conclusion rather than a promise, but its wording is not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its premise — that the Kern County Pension Plan for Physician Employees remains "a qualified alternative" — depends on Article III Section 5, which allows the Plan Document to be amended and restated subject to IRS determination; if that changed, this statement would no longer hold. It also sits beside Article II Section 1's promise that the County will pay the employer's hospital-insurance portion of Social Security ("FICA 2"), which a reader must reconcile with the blanket statement of exemption from Social Security taxes.
judgments.clause_name: Article III, 6. SOCIAL SECURITY AND MEDICARE TAXES

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Eligibility on the same basis as full-time County employees, with an express non-breach provision for plan changes. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel in form to Article III Sections 2, 4 and 8; the only outward strain is the familiar unilateral-change point already neutralised by the non-breach sentence. Nothing contradicts Article III Section 5, which excludes only other retirement plans, not deferred compensation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical drafting pattern to the deferred compensation section; eligibility, same-basis benchmark, unilateral change with non-breach language. No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No cross-reference that could conflict; consistent with the rest of Article III.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Paragraphs C, D and E are precise (a $20,000 moving cap, three-bid procedure, express cross-references). Paragraphs A and B use "approved and necessary expenditures," a standard requiring judgment, and A imposes a $2,500 annual cap while B, for education and training "as directed by KMC," carries no cap — a difference that could be argued over but is explicable by the different triggers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraphs D and E cross-refer accurately to Article II Sections 4 and 5, which do contain the professional-fee overhead deduction and other-income expense reimbursement mechanisms. Paragraph A's education reimbursement pairs with Article III Section 3.D's education leave. The references check out; nothing contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative choice of forum is left to "the KMC Faculty Practice Board policy and procedure, titled Corrective Action and Termination Review Process, or the medical staff bylaws, whichever is applicable." The disjunction plus "whichever is applicable" supplies no criterion for deciding which regime governs a given decision, and the two regimes could well differ in procedure and outcome. That is a namable indeterminacy in a provision that fixes a physician's due-process rights.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes an Article IV corrective-action/for-cause termination provision not reproduced here, and it must be squared with Article V Section 11, which preserves to the County every remedy "concurrently" and non-exclusively — a reader could take Section 11 to let the County act outside this review process. Article V Section 13's immediate-termination-on-privilege-restriction right also bypasses it. Both are reconcilable but not obviously so.
judgments.clause_name: Article IV, 3. REVIEW AND APPEAL PROCESS

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional two-sentence anti-assignment clause with an express consent carve-out for money due. "Or any part thereof" is standard and bounded by the preceding nouns.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing points outward; the direction of payments to practice groups under Article II Section 4.E is a directed distribution by the Plan Administrator rather than an assignment, so no evident conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause both requires availability "at no cost to County" and then promises that KMC "will credit the time spent in preparation and testimony as administrative time as defined in the compensation plan" — administrative time being a compensated component of base salary under Article II Section 3.A(4). The two halves of the same short paragraph pull against each other on whether the service is free. "Available ... to testify as an expert witness or otherwise" is also broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-references "administrative time as defined in the compensation plan," i.e., Article II Sections 2 and 3, under which administrative duties are compensated by base salary; and Article II Section 5.A treats "professional witness fees" as compensable other income. The interaction of a no-cost testimony obligation with those compensation provisions is the identifiable friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single clear negation of agency authority covering "any and all duties under this Agreement." No competing reading of any term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Slight friction with Exhibit A, which makes the physician a department chairman who oversees budgets, negotiates with billing services and sits on the Medical Executive Committee and Faculty Practice Board — roles that involve institutional decision-making — but those duties are internal governance rather than binding the County to third parties, so the two harmonise readily.
judgments.clause_name: Article V, 3. AUTHORITY TO BIND COUNTY

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two conventional interpretive rules stated without qualification: headings disregarded, no construction against the drafter, deemed jointly prepared. Definite in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disclaims contra proferentem while other provisions (Article V Section 11's County-only remedies clause, Section 17's County-only waiver clause) are drafted entirely in the County's favour; that makes the joint-preparation premise harder to sustain but does not contradict any operative term. Article V Section 20's recital of equal bargaining and independent review is consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: California law, performance in Kern County, venue in Kern County — all fixed and mutually consistent. No ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing outward-pointing beyond the general references to California law elsewhere (Gov. Code sections in Recital A and Article V Section 6), with which it is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific statutory references (Gov. Code §§ 1090 et seq., 87100 et seq.), a present representation of no known interest, and a defined consequence (immediate termination on written notice) if an interest existed at inception. Determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates yet another termination right outside Article IV's termination section, alongside Article V Sections 13 and 15; the proliferation is untidy but each trigger is distinct and expressly stated, so harmonisation is straightforward.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All applicable KMC and County policies and procedures" is broad and its content is set unilaterally elsewhere, and the office-policy sentence uses an open "including, but not limited to" list (orientation, case conferences, supervision, in-service education, patients' rights, performance improvement). The final sentence's obligation to submit to "other laboratory testing and physical examinations as may be required by County" is similarly open-ended. These are namable general-vs-specific features, though ordinary in an employment instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates unwritten and changeable County/KMC policy, which sits against Article V Section 22's sole-agreement clause and Article V Section 14's written-modification requirement; the daily time-sheet requirement also interacts with the hours provisions in Article II Section 1 (40 hours) and Exhibit A Sections 6 (48 hours), where the real inconsistency lies.
judgments.clause_name: Article V, 7. COMPLIANCE WITH KMC AND COUNTY POLICIES

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation is to obey "all applicable" law, followed by an "including but not limited to" list of named regimes (JCAHO, Title 22, EMTALA, HIPAA, Cal-OSHA and others). The general duty precedes the specifics, so the catch-all problem is muted — the enumeration illustrates rather than limits — but the phrase "County personnel qualifications for the practice of medicine" is an undefined standard set unilaterally.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Recital C and Article V Section 13 on licensure and staff membership. Nothing here contradicts another provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure execution boilerplate with a single, settled meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No cross-reference and no possible interaction that could generate inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two definite propositions: employment by the County under this Agreement and the medical staff bylaws, and an acknowledgment of no classified-employee or Civil Service rights. The terms "classified employee" and "Civil Service Ordinance" are external but well-defined public-law categories.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the clause where the instrument's characterisation problem surfaces. Recital A grounds the contract in Government Code section 31000, the authority to contract with specially trained persons for special services, while this section declares an employment relationship; Article II Section 2.G promises defence and indemnity "as a matter of law ... to the same extent as would be afforded to a regular full-time County employee"; Article III grants County employee benefits; yet Article IV Section 3 routes discipline through Faculty Practice Board policy or medical staff bylaws rather than County personnel process. Whether the physician is an employee, and with which employee incidents, cannot be settled from any one of these, which is a genuine whole-instrument coherence question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ownership is fixed in the County; the physician's inspection and duplication right is bounded by stated purposes (professional responsibilities, defence of claims) and by applicable law and confidentiality standards. The qualifiers are conventional and workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article V Section 8's HIPAA compliance obligation and Article V Section 2's litigation-assistance duty. Nothing indicates conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The termination sentence is in the passive voice — "This Agreement may be immediately terminated if Core Physician's privileges/membership are modified or restricted" — leaving the actor unstated, and the trigger is broad: any modification or restriction "such that services performed by Core Physician are limited or restricted," without a materiality threshold. The credentialing checklist in (a)–(d) is by contrast entirely specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It plants an immediate, notice-free termination right outside Article IV, which otherwise governs termination and, through Section 3, supplies a review and appeal process for corrective action and for-cause termination under the medical staff bylaws. Since bylaws-based restriction of privileges is precisely what Article IV Section 3's appeal machinery addresses, an immediate termination on that same event is difficult to reconcile with the review right, and it also cuts against Article IV Section 1's notice regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence requiring written, signed modifications. Standard and unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is contradicted in operation by several provisions that allow unilateral change without an amendment: Article III Section 5's "[a]ny changes in the Plan Document will control the terms of this Agreement," Article III Sections 2, 4, 7 and 8's unilateral benefit changes deemed "not a breach," and Article II Sections 2.F and 3.B's Board-set assessments and criteria. Those clauses expressly authorise their own variation, so the friction is best charged to them; hence a low-moderate score here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is oddly compound: termination "in the event insufficient funds are appropriated or budgeted for this Agreement in any fiscal year due to closing of a clinical department or KMC." It is unclear whether the closure limb qualifies the whole trigger (so ordinary budget shortfalls do not suffice) or merely illustrates a cause, and "insufficient funds ... for this Agreement" is not tied to any measurable appropriation line. The release language and 30-day notice are, by contrast, precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies a County termination right and notice period (30 days) different from Article IV Section 1.A's 90-day physician right and separate from Article V Sections 6 and 13's immediate-termination triggers, with no ordering provision among them. It also caps the County's exposure against Article II Section 1's stated five-year maximum payable. Reconcilable, but the termination architecture is scattered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence promises compliance with all anti-discrimination law and County policy; the second then enumerates protected categories — race, color, national origin, age, religion, marital status, sexual preference — omitting sex and disability, which the incorporated laws plainly cover. That is a specific list narrower than the general obligation preceding it, inviting an expressio unius argument about the contractual (as opposed to statutory) promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article V Section 8 already requires compliance with EEOC, FEHA and HIPAA obligations, which cover the omitted categories, so the general legal duty is preserved elsewhere; the mismatch is a drafting inelegance rather than a contradiction of another operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is one-sided in a way that produces an odd literal reading: "No covenant or condition of this Agreement can be waived except by the written consent of County" makes even the County's own obligations waivable only by the County, and the forbearance sentence runs solely against the physician. That is the kind of one-directional drafting that generates a construed-against-the-drafter argument, though Article V Section 4 disclaims that canon.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates and slightly extends Article V Section 11's remedies language ("entitled to invoke any remedy available to County under this Agreement or by law or in equity"), so the two must be read together; and its County-only orientation sits against Article V Section 4's joint-preparation premise and Section 20's equal-bargaining recital. No outright contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Methods of delivery, deemed-receipt rules (immediately for personal delivery, four days after deposit for mail or express) and named addresses are all fixed, with a stated mechanism for changing addresses. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the notice machinery relied on by Article IV Section 1.A (90 days' prior written notice), Article V Section 6 and Article V Section 15 (30 days' written notice); those references are consistent with it. Nothing contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A performance standard clause keyed to "accepted professional and ethical standards of the medical profession" and the medical staff bylaws — a general standard, but one with a recognised external content, and the sort of formulation courts apply routinely rather than treat as ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Recital C, Article V Sections 8 and 13, and Exhibit A's duties. No conflict indicated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recital-style acknowledgment of specialised services, mutual legal sophistication, arm's-length bargaining and independent review. It creates no obligation whose boundary must be applied, so vagueness has little bite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its heading ("RELATIONSHIP") would ordinarily fix the parties' legal relationship, which Article V Section 10 actually does and which Recital A frames differently under Government Code section 31000; a reader looking here for the employment/independent-contractor characterisation finds only bargaining recitals. The equal-bargaining premise also supports Article V Section 4's no-contra-proferentem rule, so the two are aligned rather than in conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability with the usual proviso that the remainder must still substantially constitute the intended agreement. The proviso requires judgment but is conventional and its operation is understood.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing points outward beyond its general application to every provision; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional integration clause: entire agreement including attachments, no inducements or representations other than those recited, no oral promise or modification effective. Determinate on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The instrument repeatedly incorporates and subordinates itself to documents that are not attachments — the KMC Faculty Practice Administrative Policies and Procedures Manual (Article II Section 3.B), Faculty Practice Board bylaws and assessments (Article II Section 2), the Pension Plan Document, which is said to "control the terms of this Agreement" when amended (Article III Section 5), County policies (Article III Sections 2, 4, 7, 8 and Article V Section 7), and the medical staff bylaws (Article V Sections 10 and 13). An entire-agreement clause that co-exists with several externally controlling documents is the identifiable tension, though courts routinely harmonise express incorporation with integration language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite as to role (medical director for anatomic pathology and clinical laboratories), reporting line (KMC Medical Director) and time commitment (48 hours of service, on average, per week). "On average" is softening but is given content by Exhibit A Section 6's 2112-hour annual objective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 48-hour figure directly diverges from Article II Section 1.A, which defines the same full-time commitment as "according to AMA survey data for specialty but no less than forty [40] hours per week" and fixes compensation on that basis. Exhibit A is made part of the Agreement by Article I Section 2 and Article V Section 22, so two operative texts state different weekly hours for the identical position. The reporting line to the Medical Director also sits alongside Article II Sections 2 and 3, which give the CEO and Faculty Practice Board authority over duties and compensation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sub-paragraphs a–c are tied to identifiable external standards (federal and state clinical laboratory regulation, CAP and AABB accreditation, KMC policies and medical staff bylaws). Sub-paragraph d is different: ensuring the Department "[o]perates effectively and smoothly, and provides timely reports, provided adequate resources are provided" uses three undefined measures and an escape condition ("adequate resources") with no benchmark or decision-maker, so its boundary cannot be applied as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It shares responsibility with "the laboratory manager(s)" while Exhibit A Section 2.f makes the chairman the person who evaluates the laboratory manager, and the resources proviso implicitly depends on budget decisions made under Article II Section 2.C and Exhibit A Section 2.e. These are interlocking rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but concrete enumeration of administrative duties, each with an identifiable object (policies, quality programme, CAP proficiency surveys, budgets, evaluations, named committees, monthly meetings). The soft edges are "other committees that may be assigned by the president of the medical staff" and "[c]ompletes clinical pathology and anatomic pathology service work as may be required," which are open but subordinate to a detailed list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Committee membership on the Faculty Practice Board dovetails with Article II Section 2.E, and the professional-fee documentation duty pairs with Exhibit A Section 4.b and Article II Section 4. The volume of duties bears on the 48-versus-40 hour discrepancy but does not itself contradict a provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short duties: performing anatomic pathology services "as assigned" and documenting care consistent with CMS professional-fee billing requirements. "As assigned" is open but the assignor is identifiable from the reporting structure in the Exhibit's introduction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is the paradigm open catch-all: after four sections of carefully enumerated administrative, teaching and patient-care duties, "Other duties as assigned by the chief executive officer or medical director" has no stated subject-matter limit, no volume limit and no standard of reasonableness. Whether ejusdem generis confines it to duties of the kind enumerated, or whether it is genuinely at large, cannot be resolved from the text — precisely the general-versus-specific tension the standard targets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Exhibit A Section 6's 2112-hour objective and Article II Section 1's hours and fixed compensation (assigned duties expand work without adjusting pay, and Article II Section 1.C forbids compensation adjustment absent a written amendment), and with Article II Section 3.A(5)'s base-salary category for "other activities approved by the CEO of KMC and the Faculty Practice Board" — note that section requires Board approval as well, whereas this one allows unilateral assignment by the CEO or medical director. That mismatch in who may assign compensable other activities is a real but modest inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Numerically precise and internally coherent: 48 hours per week, variation permitted week to week, and an annual objective of 2112 worked hours (which is 48 hours across 44 weeks, leaving room for the paid leave granted in Article III). "Objective" is softer than "requirement," but the figures are definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 48-hour standard workweek contradicts Article II Section 1.A's definition of the same full-time obligation as "no less than forty [40] hours per week" measured against AMA survey data, and the compensation in Article II is fixed against that 40-hour formulation. Exhibit A is incorporated by Article I Section 2 and Article V Section 22, so the instrument fixes the same variable twice at different values with no priority clause resolving which controls; Article V Section 7's daily time-sheet requirement makes the discrepancy operationally live.
